# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "In Sargasso" (Missing: A Romance), Julius Chambers, 1896
Narrator: Capt. Austin Clark, American, born Brooklyn; ex-Black Ball line apprentice; Cameron & Co. Australian ships; 1st mate then master ~27. Given command of tramp steamer **Caribas** (owners Triplett & Jones, Plymouth; ship named after Marquis of Caribas; Erie Basin NY; mahogany cabin). Crew of 40 posted "Missing" at Lloyds.

**Ch I**: Preface notes Sargasso Sea (22–28°N, 25–60°W, ~200,000 sq mi, "Harbor of Missing Ships").
**Ch II**: Sailed Harbeck's Stores, NY, June, for Azores (Horta, Ponte Delgada, Lisbon). Passenger **Arthur Gray** (claims artist; Secor launch, explosion engine). Altered course after long 40. Derelicts seen day 5. Mirage of a city of ships in eastern sky; lookout saw moving objects. Clark took launch with quadrant, chronometer, provisions. Second mate wanted to come; refused. Lost oars, engine broke.
**Ch III**: Gray took Clark's repeating rifle (Winchester). Gray steered him through canals ("redwood tree", "logwood trunk", "wire grass"). Clark's revolver empty; dropped belt of cartridges overboard. Gray: "They are my countrymen!" Landed on a derelict; snakes/insects. Kantoon (60 yrs, grizzled gray beard trimmed to 3 in., porpoise-skin dress, leather cap, stands in tub of water). Gray: ship "a fine boat... desirable accession." Clark locked in cell under deck.
**Ch IV**: Gray (shark-skin clothes, long curly brown hair) admits betrayal; was ill with smallpox, set adrift by Bermuda–Canaries schooner captain, adopted by Sargassons; Gray says crew to be given choice of joining or "mercy of extinction." Grand Kantoon "rules the sea and air." Gray says he went to US under oath.
**Ch V**: Sargasson drink (brown decoction, from plant). Kantoon speaks polyglot ("Senor Captaine... Sitzen sie down"; "Io sono the Kantoon de cette ship"). Sargasson history: began after Spanish Armada galleons; African slave ship mutineers intermarried. Ships last ~50 years. Death chant; children/rebels lashed to ship. Clark overhears plot to take Caribas.
**Ch VI**: Red light ("Sacred Fire") from locomotive headlight reflector on iron hulk; Priest of Sacred Fire. Boats: grass matting, fish-scale gum, paddles like tennis bats. Attack plan: Gray guides; tabasco-like powder and fungus drug in fish bladders; Winchester with ~6 cartridges. 200 men; 50 miles in ~8 hours; canoe-boys. Derelict hulk (listed 25°) adjacent to Caribas.
**Ch VII**: Kantoon's account: boatswain (superstitious, saw Sacred Light, omitted "eight bells", woke watch; fought with axe cutting cables; whistle). Captured; cabin boy (sweet-faced) tied and dropped overboard following second mate. Boatswain drowned in water butt on deck, at his choice. Clark's binoculars given back by Kantoon. Clark's ship now moored at distance.
**Ch VIII**: **Fidette** (Kantoon's daughter; hazel-brown eyes, reddish-brown hair; sea-grass mantle with shark-tooth clasps; rhododendron/bay sprig; wicker tray of berries; speaks Creole French). Her mother (from New Orleans, "place woman", eloped with gambler son of sugar planter; steamer **George Cornwall**, Capt. Timothy Rogers, lost 1872 Saratoga voyage; mother alone on derelict months). Kantoon claimed her as "my choice" at salvage. Clark kisses Fidette.
**Ch IX**: Kantoon angry (cabin boy saw kiss); threatens separation. Kantoon's wife died six months ago of fever. Social rules: Kantoon sole permitted wife; dry rot; barnacle-laden bark; heaven = warm water 3 ft deep; fish diet; death by drowning in D-posture; mermaids.
**Ch X**: Clark guards Fidette's swim with a spear. Visit to floating kitchen ship (cooks ~50 men; rain awning). Passed Caribas, moored in new slip.
**Ch XI**: Fidette's first love: **Don Fernandez Otranto**, son of exiled Portuguese marshal; trombone player; ship **Royal George** (Franklin's abandoned ship, rechristened **Goo-ge-Goo / Green Octopod**). Hunchbacked girl sank ship in jealousy. Trombone heard again at night — Fernandez alive.
**Ch XII**: Clark jealous; Fidette: "Week of Silence" will end before they meet.
**Ch XIII**: Week of Silence (Sun Dance; Dance of the Derelicts). Clark nearly murder-minded.
**Ch XIV**: Fernandez visits; Fidette effusive, pours water over him; Kantoon has him dropped in sack. Fidette sits with Clark, "two sympathetic octopods."
**Ch XV**: Month of the Visitation; Greek women visitors; ladies' gossip; rebellion of Chin-Goone (1816 Napoleon/St. Helena plot). Kantoon and Clark discuss in water tubs. Threat from Fernandez's crew.
**Ch XVI**: Papier-mâché orange-hued detonating bombs (Wilmington, Del., fireworks; Clark recalled Brandywine explosion). "Blood oranges." Rebel **Hansko Yap**, condemned by Kantoon for being half-inch short of six feet; used 80-ft iron-capped spar as ram; swimmers.
**Ch XVII**: Spar fight: Sargasson swimmers vs. boats; defense fails; fender used twice; Kantoon killed by a Lascar after cutting two men; Hansko's men boarding; Kantoon struck by stab in heart (Ch XIX). 
**Ch XVIII**: Fidette climbs rigging, throws four bombs into boarding square; boarders swept into sea; Fidette recaptured ship.
**Ch XIX**: Kantoon buried; Fidette and Clark marry by civil ceremony around mainmast (sprig of bay; "It is well; amen"); Fidette insists he never mention trombone man. Fidette sits with octopus on bowsprit.
**Ch XX**: Clark's boats made from roots; sea-root telegraph (grapevine telegraph, Ceylonese idea); Clark cooks chowder at night in violation of fire ban. Clark popular.
**Ch XXI**: Priest's barge **Unk-ta-hee** (60 ft) takes Clark & Fidette to Chief Kantoon's floating palace on the Inland Sea. Compass swung four points. Golden plates, orange-hued wine.
**Ch XXII**: Ceremony: Kyrie chants; High Priest of the Sacred Fire; oath with heated marlinspike; Clark named Kantoon; given Caribas by tarpon-scale token; rival commander to destroy self.
**Ch XXIII**: Return trip to Caribas; Caribas prize crew with knives; Gray found in captain's cabin, tied in chair.
**Ch XXIV**: Gray drowned in his "chair of execution" by barge commander ("Basta! ... Let him walk with God!"). Clark elevated; first mate retained. Gray had told Clark launch scuttled.
**Ch XXV**: Donna Elenora (wife of Kantoon of ship Cormorant) and Fidette start women's movement; Clark supports; mandolin song.
**Ch XXVI**: Clark gives gig to women; Cormorant's Kantoon locks wife up; women's teas with fire; jewelry bartering; Fidette's false alarm "We are lost!"
**Ch XXVII**: Sacred Flint stolen by Donna Elenora (via Fidette's careless words). Clark has crew carry ballast flint to priest; sea-root telegraph reassures Chief Kantoon.
**Ch XXVIII**: Clark plans escape: engine restore; seaweed fuel; oil from porpoises; boatswain recruited; men locked in cabins; missing sailor disappears.
**Ch XXIX**: Scissors-grinder ("Knife-Grinder's Song") collects knives; eight stokers locked; steam at 75–85 lb; sulphuric acid cleans cylinder; Clark prepared to kill crew if failure.
**Ch XXX**: Caribas steams out; Clark rams Sargasson barge (30 men killed). Sacred Fire proclaims "A Kantoonship to his captor!" Caribas fuel exhausted after two days; rode out four days; German steamer **Nordland** (Gibraltar–New York) tows to New York, anchored in the Horseshoe. Telegram from Triplett & Jones: "Austin Clark, New York: Proceed Santos, then Buenos Ayres for orders."

---

## BOOK 2: "The Templeton Case," Victor L. Whitechurch (Edward J. Clode, NY, 1924)
Setting: Marsh Quay, estuary near cathedral city **Frattenbury** (Cathedral spire, Downs), October; Mariner's Arms inn (landlady **Mrs. Yates**, widow six years); quay with Lucy (schooner; **Tom Gale**, crew/cook); opposite wood, house of **Isaac Moss** (London jewel dealer, 13a Hatton Garden; home "Fairview," 53 Compton Avenue, Brondesbury; wife Mrs. Moss; caretakers at house).

**Ch I**: Reginald Templeton arrives Saturday in cutter yacht **Firefly** (white, green line; engine). Crew **Jim Webb** (from Salcombe, employed via Jefferies). Lodger **Harold Grayson** (artist, bicycle) in Mariner's Arms bar parlour; cigar offered to Tom Gale. Templeton: explorer from Africa; posted letter at Weymouth to Canon Fittleworth.
**Ch II**: Templeton rows across to Moss's side; Gray sees Moss with Templeton; Tom points out Moss. Gray leaves at dusk.
**Ch III**: Sunday morning, Webb finds Templeton stabbed in back on yacht floor (dagger-triangular wound; died instantly). Mr. **Proctor** (bald, egg-like head, velveteen jacket, woollen slippers; neighbor; retired cigar merchant; great-nephew **Phil**). Superintendent **Norton** (black moustache); Detective-Sergeant **Colson** (alert, grey eyes; wife Bob-named "Bob", home outside city walls). Constable **Gadsden**.
**Ch IV**: Canon **Charles Fittleworth** (cathedral, daughter **Doris**, wife Mrs. Fittleworth), cousin of Templeton. Coroner **Francis Norwood** (solicitor, hatchet face, mutton-chop whiskers, never married). Canon finds **cigar band** (red and gold) on cabin floor; pockets it. Moss's housekeeper: Moss and wife left early Sunday for London (by 7.35 train).
**Ch V**: Colson: Grayson departed by bicycle; footprints/stick ferrule found by stile; Alpine ferrule. Canon's letter from A. F. Crosby (lawyer, Crosby & Paxton, 17b Lincoln's Inn Fields). Blotting-pad fragments: "...e y u on turd ft on" and "Y rs f ithfully, R. Templeton". Diamond in chamois bag. Stick found under dinghy seat.
**Ch VI**: Colson buys matching stick from Mr. **Blake** (tobacconist); wife's advice (left-handed hint). Night: Colson waits; unknown man paddles canoe to dinghy; Colson trips; canoe escapes up estuary with no paddle; Proctor's canoe found stranded.
**Ch VII**: Inquest at Mariner's Arms, Frattenbury. Proctor is foreman. Canon produces cigar band; Norwood rebukes him. Band passed round jury. Adjourned "Saturday week".
**Ch VIII**: Winnie Cotterill (illustrator, friend **Maude Wingrave**, Battersea flat) reads of murder; Templeton = her "Uncle," paid art training; mother Mabel Cotterill. Winnie stays with Fittleworths. Crosby: will leaves all to Winnie (~£2,000); Templeton's lawsuit lost, sold Buckinghamshire place to Grayson's father (Mr. Osmond Grayson, Marlow). Night: Grayson named as suspect; Winnie reacts.
**Ch IX**: Colson deductions; Tom Gale's cigar given by Grayson; band compared — same brand. Moss's identity via London letter.
**Ch X**: Grayson detained at Linderton (Constable **Drake**); Major **Renshaw** (Chief Constable). Grayson's story: sketching, Selham "Wheatsheaf" inn, shell-shock. Grayson's father's lawsuit with Templeton. Colson's "Ezra's ices" clue — Crosby reads "EZRA ICE'S".
**Ch XI**: Winnie's funeral visit; Norwood passes. Canon's list. Canon's cigar box given to police; band differs from one given at inquest (exchanged band). Mrs. Yates confirms Grayson's walking stick. Grayson released; dinner with Fittleworths; Winnie and Grayson engaged (Ch XIV).
**Ch XII**: Dinner at Norwood's: Dr. **Hazell**, Sir Peter Birchnall ("Virginian Reefs" stock), Rev. **Alfred Carringford**; Colson's thief Joe **Thatcher** (poacher) reports seeing a man row across midnight and motor-car (Merrifield's car).
**Ch XIII**: Moss confesses (diamonds: 32 stones, one missing; agent for Ehbrenstein & Co.; Hotel "Chester"); Moss's tracker Tyler. Colson's theory: Proctor (Switzerland, Julier Pass picture).
**Ch XIV**: Crosby & Winnie: she's engaged to Grayson; Templeton's sealed letter reveals: Winnie's real name **Forbes**; father **Percy Forbes**, lawyer, convicted of embezzlement, died Princetown; Templeton's £100 note.
**Ch XV**: Colson consults cigar importers; Proctor's cigar cupboard; Colson steals cigar; Proctor's lie about Switzerland. Colson's imagined reconstruction (rook).
**Ch XVI**: Proctor confesses in police room: he was driven home by Merrifield, 1:30am alibi (bridge). Proctor had switched band. Colson's "Ezra Price/Grice" and "PROOF" decoding by Crosby.
**Ch XVII**: Mrs. Colson's theories (left-handed, Frattenbury walk). Simmonds confirms stick held by middle. Buckland, chemist, recalls Ezra Grice; Norwood's old clerk.
**Ch XVIII**: Sir James Perrivale (big-game; Templeton with Ezra Grice in South Africa; Zulu medicine man). Crosby's advertisement; £50 reward; letter "hand over Ezra Grice's confession & proof. This is final."
**Ch XIX**: Crosby finds 20-year-old newspapers (embezzlement). Virginian Reefs collapse. Colson learns Juror Bailey or Westall swapped cigar band; Dean dined; Canon's Dean.
**Ch XX**: Colson accuses Norwood in Canon's house. Norwood (left-handed; stick is Norwood's; dummy stick put by Colson). Grice appears. Confession shown.
**Ch XXI**: Grice's story: Norwood embezzled, framed Forbes, Grice fled; Templeton blackmail (£10,000); Norwood's note: Templeton killed; Norwood hanged himself in cell with braces. Crosby: undecided whether to tell Winnie.

END OF NOTES.
